sn46.6:3.4: Given that this unique passage poses several linguistic difficulties, I have opted to translate it literally. | The text uses three synonyms: _citta_ (“mind”), _mānasa_ (“spirit”), and _cetasa_ (“heart”). | Read _apatitthīnacitto_ per BJT. It’s the same root as _thīna_, “sloth”. | “Undaunted spirit” (_adīnamanasa_) is also at [thag3.9:1.4]() and [thag15.1:11.4](). However, the texts waver between reading _adīna_ (“undaunted”) and _alīna_ (“not sluggish”, for which the meaning is established at [snp1.3:34.2]()). The parallel to this passed at [mnd10:92.7]() reads _alīna_ in MS, but _adīna_ in Thai and PTS editions. The commentary to the present passage glosses “mind dejected by the power of displeasure”, while the commentary at [thag3.9:1.4]() has, “non-overthrown by laziness, etc., not sluggish mind, not living lazily”.
